tasks.short: Check shift hours and pay adjustments, then post approved entries to AFAS.

today.trigger: Daily receipt of hours and adjustments from Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo; actual collection methods need confirmation.
steps: Collect submitted hours, attendance records and approved adjustments.
Match employee numbers, contracts, dates and applicable CAO rules.
Check overtime, shift allowances, missing entries and duplicates.
Ask site managers to resolve differences and approve corrections.
Post approved entries to AFAS and retain supporting records.
systems: Staffing agency portals for agency hours only
drudgery: Repeating the same checks across three sites
today.time_sinks: Likely concentrated in inconsistent submissions and late corrections; confirm against the supplied 126.1 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Import approved hours once and run repeatable checks automatically. Manual matching and rekeying disappear for clean entries.
lenses.autonomous: An approved submission triggers validation and posting; unmatched people, unexpected allowances and missing approvals enter an exception queue.
lenses.ambitious: Check every submitted shift before payroll cutoff and identify recurring submission problems by site.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet comparisons and routine chasing. Keep the satisfying work of resolving a difficult pay issue correctly.
lenses.options: Compare a proposed correction with the original entry and show its effect on hours, allowances and the processing period.
lenses.altitude: Own the rules and exception process for reliable hours rather than inspect every row.
reach: Support HR administrators with contract-to-hours checks
Help accounts payable validate agency invoice hours

tasks.human_edge: Managers confirm what happened on a shift; Payroll interprets disputed entitlements and explains corrections to employees.
tasks.pattern_why: Identity matching, duplicate detection, approved allowance rules and posting controls are checkable rules. AI can help build the integration; routine execution needs no model.

in_practice.trigger: A manager approves an hours submission or an authorised pay adjustment.
steps: Receive the submission with a unique source reference and approval record.
Validate employee identity, contract dates, CAO mapping and duplicate status.
Apply approved checks and route exceptions to the responsible site manager.
Post clean entries through a supported AFAS import or connector and reconcile accepted totals.
Record corrections separately and include totals in the payroll control pack.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers approve source hours; Payroll approves exceptions and rule changes. Final payroll release remains a separate human control.
systems: AFAS Profit supported import or connector, subject to configuration
Site attendance source, to be identified
Staffing agency portals or approved exports
data_needed: Employee and agency worker identifier mappings
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted processing log linked to AFAS posting references, source approvals, rule versions and exception decisions.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports mapping recorded hours to payroll components and approval before payroll processing; Noordhaven's configuration is unverified.
The current workflow, anatomy, 55% labour saving and 1.5 times elapsed speedup are planning assumptions, not measured results.

risks: Wrong effective dates or CAO mapping can repeat an incorrect allowance across many employees.
Retries can duplicate postings unless source references prevent double processing.
Agency hours must remain separate from Noordhaven employee payroll.

Changes to attendance monitoring or employee-data arrangements may require OR consent; assess the actual change. See [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/belangrijke-themas/privacy).
research_questions: Where are actual hours captured at each site, and can approved records be exported reliably?
What share of the 126.1 hours is manual checking beyond existing AFAS functionality?
Can three historical periods be replayed without unexplained differences in hours or allowances?
Which attendance or data-processing changes require OR involvement?

tasks.short: Calculate wages and deductions in AFAS and check the payroll before release.

today.trigger: Approved payroll inputs arrive during the month and at payroll cutoff.
steps: Collect approved salary changes, variable pay and deduction instructions.
Check effective dates and employee payroll settings.
Enter or import changes and run the AFAS provisional calculation.
Review gross-to-net differences and investigate unusual results.
Correct inputs, rerun calculations and prepare the release evidence.
today.time_sinks: Likely in input handling and review rather than arithmetic already performed by AFAS; baseline supplied is 111.2 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Feed approved changes directly into AFAS and generate a standard variance report. Avoid rebuilding wage calculations in Excel.
lenses.autonomous: An approved input batch starts validation and provisional processing where supported; failed controls stop the workflow.
lenses.ambitious: Run earlier previews so new starters and employees changing shifts can resolve pay problems before payday.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive entry and routine recalculation. Spend more time explaining unusual payslips and preventing recurring errors.
lenses.options: Use isolated AFAS previews to compare approved alternatives for a salary change, correction period or allowance treatment.
lenses.altitude: Become the owner of payroll calculation controls, configuration quality and release readiness.
reach: Support Compensation and Benefits with payroll impact calculations
Provide the Controller with payroll-to-ledger reconciliation evidence

tasks.human_edge: Payroll remains accountable for interpreting unusual deductions, disputed CAO treatment and whether a payroll is ready for release.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already performs the core calculation. The opportunity is controlled input automation and repeatable validation, with approved tax, pension and CAO configuration rather than model-generated arithmetic.

in_practice.trigger: An approved change batch is ready for a provisional payroll run.
steps: Validate input approvals, effective dates and required payroll settings.
Import changes once and reconcile accepted and rejected records.
Run provisional calculations using the maintained AFAS payroll configuration.
Produce comparisons with the prior period and approved changes.
Resolve exceptions and present the payroll control pack for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll approves every run after resolving material differences; an authorised second person approves release. Rabobank payment authorisation stays separate.
systems: Rabobank through the existing payment process
data_needed: Applicable CAO and payroll configuration versions
Current employee tax and pension settings
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS processing references and a restricted payroll control pack recording input totals, configuration versions, exceptions and approvals.

evidence.claim: AFAS provides provisional payroll checks and comparisons of calculated wage components between periods.
AFAS can journalise payroll upon approval when its financial integration is configured.
The current workflow, anatomy, 35% labour saving and 1.2 times elapsed speedup are unvalidated estimates beyond existing software automation.

risks: Automating an incorrect configuration scales the error; rule changes need approved test cases.
A plausible gross-to-net result can conceal an incorrect deduction or employee setting.
One specialist cannot provide independent approval of their own configuration, payroll and payment release.
Savings will be small if AFAS already handles most input and review work.
research_questions: Which parts of these 111.2 hours remain manual after AFAS calculation?
Can supported automation initiate provisional processing without gaining release permissions?
Which historical cases cover both CAOs, retroactive changes, pension settings and unusual deductions?
Who can independently approve payroll when the specialist is absent?

tasks.short: Keep leave and sickness balances accurate so payroll uses the right hours and pay treatment.

today.trigger: An employee requests leave, a manager records sickness or recovery, or a contract changes.
steps: Collect approved leave and authorised sickness or recovery records.
Check dates, work schedules, leave categories and overlapping entries.
Update AFAS and check entitlement calculations.
Resolve balance differences with employees, managers or HR.
Check payroll effects before cutoff.
systems: AFAS Profit leave and absence records
drudgery: Checking the same dates in several records
today.time_sinks: Likely in retrospective changes and schedule mismatches; validate against the supplied 109.8 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Use approved AFAS events to update balances and payroll inputs, removing duplicate spreadsheets and routine recalculation.
lenses.autonomous: Approved leave, recovery and contract events trigger recalculation and overlap checks; unusual cases go to HR or Payroll.
lenses.ambitious: Keep balances current throughout the month and identify first-month leave or absence coding errors before they affect a new starter's pay.
lenses.joy: Remove balance hunting and repetitive explanations. Keep sensitive conversations and fair resolution of disputed entitlements.
lenses.options: Show the balance and payroll effects of approved corrections, partial-day bookings and changed work schedules.
lenses.altitude: Own consistent leave-to-payroll rules while HR retains absence case management.
reach: Help HR administrators resolve leave record inconsistencies
Supply aggregate absence-pay reconciliation to People Analytics

tasks.human_edge: People decide disputed leave rights and sensitive absence cases; the bedrijfsarts assesses medical matters.
tasks.pattern_why: Balances, schedules, approved events and payroll mappings support explicit rules. An LLM adds little to routine bookkeeping and increases exposure of sensitive information.

in_practice.trigger: An authorised leave, sickness, recovery or contract event is recorded in AFAS.
steps: Check event dates, schedule version and approval status.
Recalculate affected leave balances using configured entitlement rules.
Detect overlaps, retrospective changes and unexplained differences.
Update permitted payroll inputs and route exceptions to the responsible person.
Reconcile balances and payroll effects at cutoff.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers approve leave; authorised HR staff record absence events. Payroll and HR approve disputed balances and exceptional pay treatment.
systems: Power BI nightly extract for retrospective aggregate reporting
data_needed: Approved leave and permitted absence events
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted AFAS change history and reconciliation log containing dates, balance movements and approvals, without diagnoses.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports converting leave and absence bookings into time entries within its payroll integration.
The current workflow, anatomy, 50% labour saving and 1.5 times elapsed speedup are planning assumptions.

risks: Incorrect schedules distort leave and payroll, especially for changing shifts and partial recovery.

Payroll should receive only necessary absence information; diagnoses and causes must not enter the workflow. See [AP rules for employers](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers).
Balance automation does not fulfil Wet verbetering poortwachter case-management obligations.
Changes to leave or absence arrangements may require OR consent. See [SER consent rights](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67).
research_questions: Are AFAS leave and absence events already integrated with payroll?
Which balance differences arise from schedules, policy interpretation or late recording?
Can the workflow operate using permitted administrative fields without medical documents?
Who owns partial-recovery coding and the separate Poortwachter process?

tasks.short: Update payroll records for approved contract changes, transfers, tax settings and departures.

today.trigger: HR approves an employee change, transfer or departure, or receives an employee's payroll declaration.
steps: Receive the approved change and its supporting record.
Check employee identity, effective date and payroll consequences.
Update AFAS contract, salary, organisational or payroll fields.
Check downstream effects and identify retrospective corrections.
Confirm completion and retain the approval evidence.
drudgery: Rekeying data already approved by HR
Finding the approval behind an entry
today.time_sinks: Likely in ambiguous instructions and retrospective changes; supplied baseline is 95.1 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Apply an approved HR change once across the relevant AFAS records. Remove separate payroll entry and manual effective-date reminders.
lenses.autonomous: An approved structured change triggers validation and a scheduled update, with exceptions held before posting.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a forward view of changes affecting the next payroll and check every departure for missing final-pay inputs.
lenses.joy: Remove copying and approval hunting. Keep the work of resolving an unusual transfer or a difficult final settlement.
lenses.options: Preview approved alternative effective dates and show which periods and payroll components they would affect.
lenses.altitude: Design reliable employee-change controls and clear ownership between HR Administration and Payroll.
reach: Help HR Administration improve change forms
Help the Controller maintain payroll cost-centre mappings

tasks.human_edge: HR authorises employment changes; Payroll challenges unclear instructions and resolves unusual tax or final-pay treatment.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured, approved changes can be validated and applied through explicit field mappings. Ambiguous email instructions should be returned for clarification rather than interpreted into live records.

in_practice.trigger: HR approves a structured employee change with an effective date.
steps: Validate required fields, approver authority and the current record version.
Check contract continuity, date conflicts and relevant payroll mappings.
Preview payroll effects and hold exceptional changes for review.
Apply approved standard changes through a supported AFAS route and read back the result.
Record before-and-after values and notify the change owner.
in_practice.human_gate: HR approves the underlying employment decision. Payroll approves retrospective changes, unusual tax treatment and final-settlement exceptions.
systems: AFAS Profit workflows and supported imports or connectors
data_needed: Employee identifier and current record version
Payroll field mappings and approval permissions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted change register linked to AFAS records, with before-and-after values, source approvals, effective dates and processing results.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents importing employee contract and salary records; exact field coverage and Noordhaven's permitted routes need verification.
The current workflow, anatomy, 55% labour saving and 1.4 times elapsed speedup are unvalidated planning assumptions.

risks: A later update can overwrite a future-dated change unless record versions and dates are checked.
US-style exemptions must be translated into relevant Dutch payroll settings, not copied literally.
Automation must apply authorised employment decisions without choosing transfers or departures.
Excessively broad connector permissions could expose or alter unrelated personnel records.
research_questions: Which changes already flow automatically from AFAS HR records into payroll?
Can the required fields be updated with effective dates and reliable read-back checks?
What proportion of changes arrives in a complete structured form?
Which departure and retrospective-change cases require specialist review?

tasks.short: Find payroll differences, trace their causes and get corrections approved.

today.trigger: A provisional payroll run, employee query or hours check reveals a discrepancy.
steps: Compare payroll results with approved hours, contracts and prior periods.
Identify unexplained differences and collect supporting records.
Trace each difference to an input, configuration or timing issue.
Agree corrections with the responsible manager or HR colleague.
Rerun affected calculations and document the resolution.
drudgery: Comparing large reports for a few meaningful differences
Searching several systems for one approval
Repeating investigations of known error types
today.time_sinks: Likely in evidence gathering and waiting for decisions; supplied baseline is 95.1 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Run rules across all payroll lines and assemble supporting evidence for each unexplained difference. Start investigations with the relevant facts together.
lenses.autonomous: Each provisional run creates exception cases and closes only differences explained by approved inputs and explicit rules.
lenses.ambitious: Check every payslip each cycle and track recurring causes so the same correction is not needed next month.
lenses.joy: Remove report scanning and document hunting. Keep investigation, judgement and helping employees receive the right pay.
lenses.options: Show alternative explanations and correction periods with their calculated consequences and supporting records.
lenses.altitude: Manage payroll quality through control coverage, unresolved cases and recurring causes.
reach: Help the Controller investigate payroll-to-ledger differences
Help People Analytics measure payroll error causes

tasks.human_edge: A person decides whether evidence establishes an entitlement and handles disputed underpayments, recoveries and sensitive employee conversations.
tasks.pattern_why: Investigation crosses records and involves exceptions. Deterministic checks find differences; an optional LLM can summarise permitted evidence, while Payroll approves every proposed correction.

in_practice.trigger: A provisional payroll run finishes or a discrepancy case is opened.
steps: Compare current results with approved inputs, prior results and explicit control rules.
Collect relevant records within the case owner's access rights.
Prepare an evidence-linked explanation and proposed correction using deterministic calculations.
Ask Payroll to approve, reject or request more evidence.
Apply the approved correction, rerun checks and retain the resolution.
in_practice.human_gate: Payroll approves every correction; the appropriate manager or HR owner confirms disputed source facts. The workflow cannot decide employee fault or authorise deductions.
systems: Approved enterprise LLM endpoint, optional and subject to data controls
Power BI for historical reporting only
data_needed: Permitted supporting records and correction history
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted discrepancy register recording control results, evidence references, proposed and approved actions, model version if used, and rerun results.

evidence.claim: AFAS provides wage-component comparisons across periods and checks before payroll approval.
An LLM can plausibly draft evidence-linked summaries, but reliable investigation across Noordhaven's records is unproven.
The current workflow, anatomy, 45% labour saving and 1.3 times elapsed speedup are planning assumptions.

risks: An apparently reasonable explanation can conceal missing evidence or an incorrect rule.
Historic errors can become accepted baselines if checks only compare periods.
Documents can contain malicious instructions; any LLM must treat retrieved text as evidence, with no posting authority.

If AI evaluates workers or influences employment terms, assess EU AI Act classification for that intended use; a human gate alone does not settle it. See [European Commission employment guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/recital-57).
research_questions: Which discrepancy types account for most investigation time and financial impact?
Can rules find known historical errors without overwhelming Payroll with false alarms?
Can every proposed explanation cite accessible, authoritative evidence?
Does the intended AI use remain evidence preparation, or influence decisions affecting employment terms?

tasks.short: Complete arrival and departure records and resolve missing shift entries.

today.trigger: A shift ends or a site submits incomplete attendance records.
steps: Collect available arrival and departure entries from the site.
Identify missing pairs, overlaps and shifts crossing midnight.
Ask the employee or supervisor to confirm missing facts.
Complete the timesheet with the approved actual times.
Submit the record for approval and payroll processing.
systems: AFAS Profit where hours are recorded
drudgery: Finding missing arrival or departure entries
today.time_sinks: Likely dominated by missing factual records and shift-boundary corrections; supplied baseline is 84 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Pair available timestamps and prepare timesheets automatically. People only supply missing facts and resolve ambiguous entries.
lenses.autonomous: A completed shift triggers pairing and validation; incomplete records generate a focused correction request.
lenses.ambitious: Resolve attendance gaps after each shift so they do not accumulate into a payroll-cutoff problem.
lenses.joy: Remove timestamp copying and repetitive chasing. Keep direct resolution of disputed records.
lenses.options: Present the original timestamps, roster and reported correction together so a supervisor can assess the evidence.
lenses.altitude: Own attendance-record quality and the process for correcting missing facts.
reach: Support site supervisors with attendance completion reports
Help agency coordinators resolve missing agency timesheets

tasks.human_edge: Employees and supervisors establish actual attendance. A roster or inferred timestamp cannot substitute for a missing fact.
tasks.pattern_why: Timestamp pairing and completeness checks are rules. Missing attendance requires confirmation, not generative completion.

in_practice.trigger: A shift closes and timestamp records become available.
steps: Retrieve source timestamps with employee identifiers and local time information.
Pair entries and check overlaps, midnight crossings and daylight-saving changes.
Create complete draft timesheets and flag missing or ambiguous facts.
Obtain authorised corrections and manager approval.
Pass approved records to hours validation without duplicate submission.
in_practice.human_gate: Supervisors approve actual times and all missing-entry corrections. Routine pairing can run automatically; it must never invent arrival or departure times.
systems: Existing site attendance source, to be identified
AFAS Profit or the approved hours-entry route
data_needed: Original timestamps and source record identifiers
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted attendance correction log preserving original timestamps, corrected values, reasons, approvers and export references.

evidence.claim: Timestamp pairing, missing-entry checks and duplicate prevention are established deterministic processing techniques.
The current workflow, anatomy, 50% labour saving and 1.4 times elapsed speedup are unvalidated; no attendance platform was specified.

risks: A roster, access-card event or planned break does not necessarily prove payable working time.
Automatic rounding or break deductions can reduce pay incorrectly.
New or changed attendance monitoring may require OR consent. See [SER employee privacy guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/belangrijke-themas/privacy).
Biometrics or continuous location tracking would introduce a separate, materially different proposal.
research_questions: What currently records actual arrival and departure times at each site?
How often are entries missing, and how long do confirmations take?
Which approved rules govern breaks, rounding, overnight shifts and daylight-saving changes?
Can existing records support this workflow without adding new monitoring?

tasks.short: Get new starters into AFAS payroll correctly before their first payday.

today.trigger: A signed employment agreement and approved starter notification reach HR and Payroll.
steps: Collect the signed contract, employee details and required payroll declarations.
Check completeness and coordinate authorised identity verification.
Check start date, salary, hours, CAO and payroll settings.
Create or complete the AFAS employee and payroll records.
Check the first payroll preview and chase unresolved items.
drudgery: Checking whether HR or Payroll completed each step
today.time_sinks: Likely in incomplete handovers and late documents; supplied baseline is 78.7 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Collect starter data through a secure structured form and reuse approved contract fields. Payroll reviews exceptions and the first-pay preview.
lenses.autonomous: A signed-contract handover creates a checklist, validates required fields and prepares the AFAS record; incomplete items remain visible.
lenses.ambitious: Give every new employee a checked first-pay preview before cutoff, reducing avoidable payroll problems during their first 90 days.
lenses.joy: Remove rekeying and repeated document chasing. Keep welcoming people and explaining their first payslip.
lenses.options: Show the actual contract's first-pay outcome under the approved start date and payroll cutoff, including any expected later correction.
lenses.altitude: Own first-pay readiness across recruitment, HR Administration and Payroll.
reach: Coordinate the payroll part of HR Administration's starter checklist
Give recruiters a clear view of payroll handover completeness

tasks.human_edge: Authorised staff verify identity and contractual facts; Payroll resolves unusual tax, pension or cross-border situations.
tasks.pattern_why: Onboarding combines documents, structured fields, reminders and system writes. Optional document extraction can prepare checkable fields, but authorised staff approve each starter before payroll activation.

in_practice.trigger: HR confirms a signed contract and authorises payroll onboarding.
steps: Create a starter case from the authorised handover using only necessary recruitment fields.
Collect sensitive payroll details through a restricted form and validate completeness.
Prepare contract and payroll fields, using optional extraction with document references for review.
Have HR confirm identity and contract details and Payroll approve payroll settings.
Create or complete AFAS records once and run a first-pay preview.
in_practice.human_gate: HR confirms identity verification and signed terms; Payroll approves every new payroll record. Bank-detail changes require an independent verification process.
systems: Recruitee handover through a supported route, to be verified
AFAS Profit supported import or connector
Restricted Microsoft 365 form and personnel storage
data_needed: Signed contract and authorised starter approval
Verified identity status and required payroll identifiers
Securely supplied bank details and payroll declarations
Start date, hours, salary, CAO and relevant payroll settings
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted starter case linked to AFAS, recording document references, field verification, approvals and first-pay checks; mask bank details and BSN in operational logs.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports employee imports and checks whether people and employee records already exist.
Document extraction can plausibly prepare starter fields for review; it does not establish identity or contractual validity.
The current workflow, anatomy, 60% labour saving and 1.5 times elapsed speedup are planning assumptions; no Recruitee-to-AFAS integration is assumed installed.

risks: Extraction errors in salary, hours, dates or bank details can affect the first payment.
BSN, identity documents and bank details must not be copied into broad Teams channels or general model prompts.
A hired pipeline stage alone does not prove a signed contract or approved payroll instruction.
Agency workers belong in the agency process unless Noordhaven becomes their employer.
research_questions: Which starter fields are already captured once and transferred to AFAS?
Can Recruitee provide a reliable authorised handover without transferring unnecessary candidate material?
What proportion of starters misses payroll readiness because of missing data versus approval delays?
Can a pilot reduce first-pay errors while retaining identity and bank-detail verification?

tasks.short: Bring approved hours and payroll inputs together into one reconciled batch.

today.trigger: Daily or weekly submissions arrive, followed by the payroll cutoff.
steps: Collect approved timesheets, variable-pay records and relevant production totals.
Match worker identifiers, dates and payroll periods.
Convert source formats into payroll input categories.
Reconcile source totals and separate agency records.
Prepare the batch for validation and payroll import.
systems: Site time and production sources, not specified
today.time_sinks: Likely in file preparation and inconsistent identifiers; supplied baseline is 78.1 hours a year.

lenses.faster: Use repeatable imports and mappings to replace file downloads, copy-paste and monthly spreadsheet rebuilding.
lenses.autonomous: An approved source file or supported feed triggers ingestion, reconciliation and a ready-or-blocked batch status.
lenses.ambitious: Provide daily completeness by site and worker group so missing inputs are fixed before cutoff.
lenses.joy: Remove file wrangling and repeated totals. Keep improving input quality with site colleagues.
lenses.options: Compare alternative cutoff dates and identify which approved inputs would move into the following period without changing records.
lenses.altitude: Own the reliability and traceability of payroll inputs across three sites and three agencies.
reach: Provide reconciled agency-hour evidence to accounts payable
Provide agreed labour-hour totals to FP&A and People Analytics

tasks.human_edge: People determine which sources are authoritative, approve new mappings and resolve disputed or missing submissions.
tasks.pattern_why: Structured collection, mapping, deduplication and control totals are repeatable data processing. AI can help implement adapters; the production pipeline should run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: An approved source submission arrives or a scheduled supported export becomes available.
steps: Ingest approved files or feeds with source references and timestamps.
Validate schemas, worker identifiers, period coverage and duplicate status.
Map approved categories while keeping employee and agency records separate.
Reconcile row counts, hours and amounts against source totals and quarantine failures.
Publish a versioned batch for downstream validation and controlled AFAS import.
in_practice.human_gate: Source owners approve submissions; Payroll approves new mappings and resolves failed reconciliations. Clean batches proceed automatically without granting payroll-release authority.
systems: Agency portal supported exports or APIs, availability to be confirmed
Power BI nightly extract for historical reporting
data_needed: Approved source records and source totals
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted ingestion register containing source references, batch versions, mappings, control totals, rejected rows and downstream import receipts.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports integrating recorded time into payroll through configured mappings; external source adapters still require verification.
The current workflow, anatomy, 65% labour saving and 2 times elapsed speedup are unvalidated planning assumptions.

risks: A portal layout or export-schema change can silently alter the meaning of a column.
Reprocessed files can duplicate hours unless batches and source records have stable identifiers.
Power BI's nightly refresh is unsuitable as the live authority for cutoff decisions.
Production data should enter payroll only where an approved pay rule requires it; individual performance scoring would be a separate use.
research_questions: Which sites and agencies provide stable machine-readable exports or supported APIs?
Are production figures actually used in pay calculations, and under which approved rules?
Can source totals and worker identities be reconciled without unexplained differences?
How much compilation work overlaps with attendance completion, validation and discrepancy investigation?

role.altitude: Payroll control and service owner: maintain reliable inputs, approved calculation rules, clear exceptions and a dependable first payday across all three sites.
reach: Coordinate first-pay readiness with Recruiters and HR Administrators
Support Compensation and Benefits with controlled payroll previews
Supply payroll-to-ledger evidence to the Controller and Accountants
Supply reconciled agency hours to accounts payable without taking over agency payroll
Improve shared payroll data definitions with People Analytics and the HRIS Analyst
role.ceiling_note: These tasks total 778.1 supplied hours, about 48.6% of a 1,600-hour role. Today's workflows and anatomy are inferred. Savings estimate human labour released; speedups estimate elapsed completion including remaining approvals. Both require measurement against current AFAS use. Shared collection, validation and reconciliation improvements must not be counted twice. Released time at EUR 55/hour is capacity value, not automatic cash savings; one-person payroll still needs cover and independent release approval.
skills_to_grow: AFAS payroll configuration, supported imports and connector permissions
Effective-dated CAO rules and payroll regression testing
Data reconciliation, duplicate prevention and exception analysis
Clear payslip explanations and handling disputed pay
AVG/GDPR data minimisation and restricted operational logging
OR consultation and intended-use assessment for any employment-related AI
Measuring first-pay accuracy, approval delays and recurring error causes
role.ambitious_version: Run a continuously checked payroll service that resolves problems before payday and gives every new starter a verified first-pay preview. Track first-pay accuracy alongside 90-day retention to test its contribution to hire-to-productive, while keeping employment judgement, sensitive conversations and payment approval with accountable people.
